ev.t_road_robbers.title: Ambush on the Road
ev.t_road_robbers.text: On an empty stretch of road five men step out of the bushes with clubs and knives. One grabs you by the shoulder, another is already rummaging through your packs. Their leader, a scar running down his cheek, smiles almost kindly: “Your purse, and go in peace.”
ev.t_road_robbers.text.rome: On a deserted stretch of road between two roadside tombs, five men climb over a wall with clubs and knives - runaway slaves or ruined shepherds, there's no telling. Their leader, a scar running down his cheek, smiles almost kindly: “Your purse, and go in peace.”
ev.t_road_robbers.text.egypt: The caravan fell behind, and on the empty road between villages five men on donkeys surround you, armed with sticks and sickles. Their leader, a scar running down his cheek, smiles almost kindly: “Your purse, and go in peace.”
ev.t_road_robbers.hand_over.ok: They took your purse, your cloak, even your shoes. You limped home barefoot, counting every stone and every loss.
ev.t_road_robbers.fight.success: You grabbed a stick and knocked the first one flat. The rest scattered, but the leader looked back as he ran and memorized your face. You memorized his.
ev.t_road_robbers.fight.failure: There were too many. You woke in a ditch with a cracked head and no money - and, for some reason, wearing someone else's hat.
ev.t_road_robbers.bluff: Say soldiers are right behind you
ev.t_road_robbers.bluff.success: You waved so confidently at the dust beyond the bend that the robbers exchanged looks and melted into the brush. The dust turned out to be an old woman with a bundle of firewood.
ev.t_road_robbers.bluff.failure: The leader laughed. “Soldiers? Out here?” For the lie they took twice as much - your purse and a beating.
ev.t_road_robbers.flee.success: You ran until your lungs gave out. The packs are gone, but the purse inside your tunic is safe.
ev.t_road_robbers.flee.failure: One of them caught you at a stream. The purse followed the packs, and the bruises stayed with you.
ev.t_robbers_caught.title: The Gang Is Caught
ev.t_robbers_caught.text: The robbers from the road have been caught. You're summoned to identify them and reclaim what's left of the loot. Among the bound men is a boy of thirteen who went through your packs that day. He looks at you and says nothing.
ev.t_robbers_caught.identify.ok: You pointed at each of them. Some of your goods came back, and the trial was short. You lay awake that night - but justice is justice.
ev.t_robbers_caught.spare_boy.ok: The boy was let go. A month later he turned up at your door asking for work - and he's followed you like a shadow ever since.
ev.t_night_burglary.title: The Hole in the Wall
ev.t_night_burglary.text: A draft wakes you: there's a gaping hole in the storeroom wall, and the chest with your savings for a rainy day is gone. Hurried footsteps still echo down the street. Years of saving are in someone else's hands.
ev.t_night_burglary.text.athens: A draft wakes you: “wall-diggers” have tunneled through the mud-brick wall of your storeroom, and the chest with your savings for a rainy day is gone. Hurried footsteps still echo down the street. Years of saving are in someone else's hands.
ev.t_night_burglary.chase.success: You caught up with them in an alley: the chest is heavy and thieves aren't strongmen. They dropped it and fled with only a handful.
ev.t_night_burglary.chase.failure: In the dark you tripped over a basket and smashed your knee. The footsteps faded, and with them everything you'd saved.
ev.t_night_burglary.curse: Pay for a curse on the thief
ev.t_night_burglary.curse.ok: A wise woman muttered over your threshold - “May whoever took it neither sleep nor eat until it is returned” - and buried a little bundle of ashes at the crossroads. It hasn't brought the money back, but you sleep better.
ev.t_night_burglary.accuse.success: You were right: the chest turned up at a fence your neighbor did business with. Nearly all of it came back.
ev.t_night_burglary.accuse.failure: The suspicion was empty, the offense was real. No money - and a neighbor who now hates you.
ev.t_night_burglary.accept.ok: You patched the wall and decided: from now on your money stays with people you can trust, not in a storeroom. An expensive lesson, but you'll never forget it.
ev.t_burglar_returns.title: The Thief Pays Back
ev.t_burglar_returns.text: In the morning there was a pouch of money on your doorstep, and a neighbor's boy passed on a stranger's message: “Lift the curse. I can't take any more.” The wise woman knew her business, it seems.
ev.t_pirates_recognized.title: A Face from Home
ev.t_pirates_recognized.text: In the market a merchant stares at you - and goes pale. “You're from our town! I knew your family!” You were born free, kidnapped by pirates, and now there's someone who can swear to it.
ev.t_pirates_recognized.plead: Beg him to buy your freedom
ev.t_pirates_recognized.plead.ok: The merchant paid your master and took you home. You're free, but you owe him a great deal - and you'll be paying it back for years.
ev.t_pirates_recognized.sue.success: The merchant swore before the judge that he'd known you since childhood. A free person kidnapped can't be held as a slave: your master had to let you go.
ev.t_pirates_recognized.sue.failure: Your master brought witnesses of his own, and the court didn't believe one merchant. At home a beating and harder work were waiting.
ev.t_shipwreck.title: Shipwreck
ev.t_shipwreck.text: The storm struck at night. The mast snapped, the ship heeled over, and water poured into the hold. The cargo is going down, people are screaming, and toward the shore - are those lights, or stars?
ev.t_shipwreck.vow: Pray to heaven and make a vow
ev.t_shipwreck.vow.success: You swore an offering if you lived - and a wave threw you onto a sandbar right at the feet of fishermen. Now the vow must be kept.
ev.t_shipwreck.vow.failure: Heaven heard, but took its time: you drifted two days on a broken spar. You survived - battered, with a vow on your heart.
ev.t_shipwreck.help.success: You pulled three people out of the water, among them a wealthy merchant. He swore he'd never forget that night - and he seemed to mean it.
ev.t_shipwreck.help.failure: You couldn't hold on to the last one, and you swallowed seawater and smashed your arm against the hull. You lived by a miracle.
ev.t_shipwreck.swim.success: The lights were a fishing village. You crawled ashore before dawn, shaking and laughing at being alive.
ev.t_shipwreck.swim.failure: The current dragged you away from shore all night. You were picked up half-dead, and your health has never been the same.
ev.t_shipwreck.strongbox.success: You hauled the chest onto a piece of mast and didn't let go until you reached land. The cargo is lost, but the money is with you.
ev.t_shipwreck.strongbox.failure: The chest dragged you under. You let go at the last moment - no money, but alive.
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.title: The Vow
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.text: You dreamed of the sea again, and a voice reminded you: you promised an offering for your rescue. At the shrine the keeper nodded as if he'd been expecting you. “Heaven is patient, but it has a long memory.”
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.pay.ok: You ordered a little silver ship for the shrine and fed the poor of the whole quarter. It felt like shedding a sodden cloak.
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.tablet.ok: The tablet shows a sinking ship and you clinging to a spar. Modest but honest - the shrine has hundreds like it.
ev.t_shipwreck_vow.forget.ok: You decided you swam out on your own. The neighbors shake their heads, and you've avoided the sea ever since.
ev.t_buried_treasure.title: Buried Treasure
ev.t_buried_treasure.text: Your hoe clanks against something hard. Under the clods is a clay pot full of old silver and jewelry, dark with age. Someone buried it during a long-ago war and never came back. Across the boundary, your neighbor is watching.
ev.t_buried_treasure.report: Report the find to the authorities
ev.t_buried_treasure.report.ok: The treasure was divided according to the law, and your share is still more than you've seen in your whole life. The whole district talks about your honesty.
ev.t_buried_treasure.keep.ok: You reburied the pot under the hearth and spend a little at a time so no one notices. Only your neighbor has become suspiciously friendly.
ev.t_buried_treasure.temple.ok: The keepers of the shrine accepted the gift gratefully and set aside a small share for you. The earth gave back to the holy what was never hers - so the village says.
ev.t_buried_treasure.share.ok: You divided the find right there on the boundary. Now you have money - and someone who keeps the same secret.
ev.t_treasure_informer.title: Informed On
ev.t_treasure_informer.text: Someone has informed on you about the treasure. An official arrives with guards. “Concealing a find is a crime. Where is the treasure?”
ev.t_treasure_informer.pay: Hand it over and pay the fine
ev.t_treasure_informer.pay.ok: You had to give up almost everything left, and more besides. The wealth went as fast as it came.
ev.t_treasure_informer.deny.success: They found nothing under the hearth - you'd moved the pot long ago. The official left empty-handed, but the rumors stayed.
ev.t_treasure_informer.deny.failure: They found the pot, and for lying the fine was doubled. The neighbors greet you through clenched teeth now.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.title: News of an Inheritance
ev.t_distant_inheritance.text: A messenger brings news: in a distant city a distant relative of yours has died childless - a man you never met. By his last wishes everything is yours: house, workshop, household. And debts, which no one can put a number to.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.text.rome: A messenger brings a will sealed by seven witnesses: in a distant city a distant relative of yours has died childless. Everything is yours - on condition that you take his name and honor his tomb. And debts, which no one can put a number to.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.accept.success: The debts were small and the house is in the best part of town. Suddenly you're a person of means.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.accept.failure: The creditors descended like gulls. The debts ate the inheritance, and you had to pay the rest out of your own pocket.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.sell_rights: Sell your claim to a speculator
ev.t_distant_inheritance.sell_rights.ok: A shrewd speculator paid good money for the claim. How much he made himself, you'd rather not know.
ev.t_distant_inheritance.give_away: Give it to his poor relatives
ev.t_distant_inheritance.give_away.ok: You renounced it in favor of his brother's widow and her children. She wept and kissed your hands, and the story spread through two cities.
ev.t_inheritance_contest.title: A Contested Inheritance
ev.t_inheritance_contest.text: A distant cousin of the deceased has turned up claiming witnesses to another, later set of last wishes. The witnesses are suspiciously well fed and remember it all suspiciously well.
ev.t_inheritance_contest.court.success: The judge questioned the witnesses separately, and each remembered a different day and different weather. The lie was thrown out; the inheritance is yours.
ev.t_inheritance_contest.court.failure: The court believed the witnesses. Half the inheritance went to the impostor, and you made an enemy.
ev.t_inheritance_contest.settle: Split it to avoid a lawsuit
ev.t_inheritance_contest.settle.ok: You divided the property before witnesses. Galling, but peaceful.
ev.t_patron_returns.title: Back from Exile
ev.t_patron_returns.text: Your old patron has returned: the charges dropped, part of the property restored. The first person he sent for was you. “You alone didn't turn away. One doesn't forget that.” In his hands is a heavy purse.
ev.t_denounce_shame.title: The Son Remembers
ev.t_denounce_shame.text: The son of the man you once testified against has grown up. In the middle of the market, loudly, he reminded everyone how you paid for your comfort. Now you have an enemy for life.
ev.t_speech_fame.title: The Voice of the Crowd
ev.t_speech_fame.text: You never meant to speak - you just couldn't stand it when the crowd started slandering an honest man. The words came on their own; people laughed at first, then fell silent, then roared. By morning there were people waiting at your door.
ev.t_speech_fame.text.athens: On the Pnyx you never meant to speak - you just couldn't stand it when they started slandering an honest man. The words came on their own; the Assembly laughed at first, then fell silent, then roared. By morning there were people waiting at your door.
ev.t_speech_fame.politics.success: You threw banquets, spoke on every corner - and became a man to be reckoned with. The powerful now seek your friendship.
ev.t_speech_fame.politics.failure: The second speech was worse than the first; the third was jeered. The money for banquets is gone, and the fame was shorter than a festival.
ev.t_speech_fame.mouthpiece.ok: A rich man pays you to say his words. He pays well. The words do sometimes stick in your throat.
ev.t_speech_fame.back_to_work: Go back to your own work
ev.t_speech_fame.back_to_work.ok: You waved off the offers. The fame faded in a month; your neighbors' respect remained.
ev.t_fame_enemies.title: Old Words
ev.t_fame_enemies.text: The man you once mocked in a speech hasn't forgotten. Now he's rich, and he's taken you to court - for slander and anything else he could think of.
ev.t_fame_enemies.defend.success: You made the crowd laugh again - at him, again. The suit was dismissed and your fame flared up anew.
ev.t_fame_enemies.defend.failure: This time the words didn't come. The court fined you, and this time they laughed at you.
ev.t_fame_enemies.pay_off.ok: He took the money and dropped the suit. He won - but at least quietly.
ev.t_friend_betrays.title: The Surety
ev.t_friend_betrays.text: You stood surety for {npc} when {g=npc_sex:he|she} needed a large loan. Now {npc} has vanished with the money, and the lender is at your door with the witnesses who heard you give your word.
ev.t_friend_betrays.pay.ok: You gave up half of everything you had. The lender left satisfied, and you no longer speak the name {npc}.
ev.t_friend_betrays.chase.success: You found the runaway at an inn two days' journey away, already packed to move on. Nearly all the money came back. The friendship didn't.
ev.t_friend_betrays.chase.failure: The runaway left an hour before you arrived, and the trail went cold. The journey cost plenty, and the debt is still yours.
ev.t_friend_betrays.deny.success: No witnesses turned up and the court left you alone. But people remember that you went back on your word.
ev.t_friend_betrays.deny.failure: The lender produced two witnesses. You paid with interest - and got a liar's name into the bargain.
ev.t_friend_returns.title: The Prodigal Debtor
ev.t_friend_returns.text: The one you stood surety for has come back - gray-haired, in an expensive cloak. He stands at your door holding a purse and can't raise his eyes. “I made my fortune in distant lands. Here's everything I owe you, and more.”
ev.t_friend_returns.take.ok: You counted it all in front of him. Every last bit. The debt is closed - and nothing more.
ev.t_friend_returns.forgive.ok: You sat up until morning, remembering your youth. Not every friendship can be saved, but this one was.
ev.t_friend_returns.drive_away.ok: You shut the door without taking a thing. Pride is capital too.
ev.t_uncover_crime.title: Someone Else's Secret
ev.t_uncover_crime.text: Late one evening you happen to see the steward carrying out sacks of the master's grain and rewriting the accounts. He looks up - and realizes you saw everything. “Surely we can come to an arrangement,” he says quietly.
ev.t_uncover_crime.report.success: The owner checked the accounts and threw the thief out. You were rewarded and trusted more than ever.
ev.t_uncover_crime.report.failure: The steward got there first: you were blamed for the theft. You had to pay and explain yourself, and now you have an enemy.
ev.t_uncover_crime.report_master.success: The master counted the sacks himself and went pale. The thief was sold to the quarries, and the master took notice of you - perhaps more notice than you think.
ev.t_uncover_crime.report_master.failure: The master believed the steward, not a slave. You were flogged for slander, and the steward now watches you like a wolf.
ev.t_uncover_crime.blackmail: Take a share for your silence
ev.t_uncover_crime.blackmail.ok: Now once a month he silently slips you a little pouch of money. You both know it won't last forever.
ev.t_uncover_crime.silent.ok: You pretended you saw nothing. Only now it's hard to look him in the eye - or yourself.
ev.t_blackmail_turns.title: The Thief Rises
ev.t_blackmail_turns.text: The steward you kept quiet about for years has bought his freedom, grown rich and made friends. Now he wants the witness gone. “Give back everything you took - or you'll regret it.”
ev.t_blackmail_turns.pay.ok: You gave back all of it and more. The old secret has finally stopped being worth money.
ev.t_blackmail_turns.expose.success: The old accounts survived, and the court believed them. The thief was convicted and you were rewarded as a witness.
ev.t_blackmail_turns.expose.failure: He had friends among the judges. You were beaten in an alley, and the city calls you an extortionist.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.title: Your {g=npc_sex:Son|Daughter} Is Missing
ev.t_child_kidnapped.text: {npc} didn't come home from the market. A fisherman saw a child being led to a slave trader's ship moored at the far quay. The ship sails with the evening wind.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.chase.success: You stormed up the gangplank with a scream you wouldn't have recognized as your own. The traders didn't want trouble: {npc} is home again and asleep, holding your hand.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.chase.failure: The ship was already pulling away. You ran along the quay until it vanished into the dusk. You never saw {g=npc_sex:him|her} again.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.ransom.success: The go-between took the money, and within the hour {npc} was in your arms. You walked home in silence and didn't let go for a moment.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.ransom.failure: The go-between took the money and disappeared. The ship sailed with the evening wind.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.magistrate.success: The watch closed the harbor and searched the ship. {npc} was in the hold among other people's children - terrified, but alive.
ev.t_child_kidnapped.magistrate.failure: While the watchmen were gathering, the ship slipped away. The official spread his hands: the sea is large.
ev.t_lost_child_news.title: News from Afar
ev.t_lost_child_news.text: Many years later a letter comes from a distant city. The child stolen from you is alive: a kind master set them free, and they have a family and a trade of their own. At the end, in an unpracticed hand: “I remember your voice.”
ev.t_lost_child_news.send_money.ok: You sent a purse with a merchant, along with a letter it took you three nights to write. For the first time in years, you breathe easier.
ev.t_lost_child_news.go_see.ok: The journey was long. You didn't recognize each other at first - and then you talked until dawn.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.title: You Are Being Sold
ev.t_slave_sold_away.text: Your master is drowning in debt and selling off part of the household. A contractor who buys people for the hardest labor has already inspected you - no one comes back from there young. The sale is set for tomorrow.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.text.athens: Your master is drowning in debt and selling off part of the household. A contractor from the Laurion silver mines has already inspected you - no one comes back from there young. The sale is set for tomorrow.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.text.rome: Your master is drowning in debt and selling off part of the household. The steward of a vast estate, where slaves work in chains and sleep in a cellar, has already inspected you. The sale is set for tomorrow.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.text.egypt: Your master is drowning in debt and selling off part of the household. A contractor for the royal quarries in the eastern desert has already inspected you - no one comes back from there young. The sale is set for tomorrow.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.plead: Throw yourself at your master's feet
ev.t_slave_sold_away.plead.success: Your master remembered your years of service and sold some of his own goods instead. You stay - for now.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.plead.failure: Your master turned away. In the morning you were led off in a column, and life became twice as hard.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.show_skill: Show the buyers what you can do
ev.t_slave_sold_away.show_skill.ok: In front of the buyers you tallied the whole stock in your head and named the price of every item. The steward of a rich household, who'd come for a cook, outbid the contractor - and took you to the city instead of the hard labor.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.run.success: You climbed the wall and followed a streambed so the dogs would lose the scent. Somewhere ahead lie a new name and a free life.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.run.failure: The dogs found you by morning. For a runaway: a brand, and the hardest work there is.
ev.t_slave_sold_away.accept.ok: You went without a word. The work is brutal, but you endure - and the overseers are starting to notice.
ev.t_overseer_chance.title: The Whip in Your Hand
ev.t_overseer_chance.text: The old overseer has died, and the steward picked you. “You're tough and you don't whine. You'll watch the others.” Better food, lighter work - but you'll have to raise the whip against your own.
ev.t_overseer_chance.take.ok: Now you have a corner of your own and an extra bowl of stew. And looks you can't hide from.
ev.t_overseer_chance.refuse.ok: The steward shrugged and chose someone else. The work stays the same, but the others in the barracks now share their last crust with you.
ev.t_slave_born_free.title: You Were Born Free
ev.t_slave_born_free.text: A dying old slave woman called you over one night and whispered: you were stolen as a baby from a free family in the next town; she remembers the family's name and the street. Which means that by law you shouldn't be a slave at all.
ev.t_slave_born_free.sue.success: A free man agreed to plead your cause, and old witnesses confirmed the story. The court declared you freeborn.
ev.t_slave_born_free.sue.failure: Your master called it an old woman's ravings, and the court agreed. Now he looks at you as an enemy.
ev.t_slave_born_free.search_family: Secretly send word to the family
ev.t_slave_born_free.search_family.ok: You begged a traveling peddler to carry the old woman's words to the next town. Now all you can do is wait.
ev.t_slave_born_free.silent.ok: You buried the old woman and her secret with her. But at night you think about an unknown street in the next town.
ev.t_born_free_family.title: A Brother
ev.t_born_free_family.text: A stranger with your eyes stands at the gate. “They've been waiting for you at home all these years,” he says. “I've saved enough to buy you out. Let's go home.”
ev.t_born_free_family.go.ok: Your master took the money, and you walked out of the gate free. You have a brother, a home, and the name you were given at birth.
ev.t_born_free_family.stay.ok: Your people are here - the ones you've shared bread and grief with. Your brother left in tears, promising to come back.
ev.t_slave_saves.title: A Child in the River
ev.t_slave_saves.text: The master's son slipped on the jetty and fell into the river. The current is carrying him fast toward a whirlpool; the nurse is screaming, and everyone else is frozen on the bank.
ev.t_slave_saves.rush.success: You dragged the boy ashore alive. The master wept as he held his son, and a week later, before witnesses, he declared you free.
ev.t_slave_saves.rush.failure: A fisherman in a boat pulled the boy out, and the current smashed you against the rocks. The master is grateful, but gave you no freedom.
ev.t_slave_saves.call_help.ok: The boatmen pulled the boy out. The master noticed you kept your head - and that's all.
ev.t_slave_saves.use_chaos.success: Everyone was watching the river, and you slipped into the reeds and never came back. They say the boy was saved. They're still looking for you.
ev.t_slave_saves.use_chaos.failure: You were caught before sunset. A runaway who left a child to drown - the master won't forgive that.
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.title: Two Roads to Freedom
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.text: The freedman potter across the street would give all his savings to buy you and make you his wife. And your master, a widower, hinted yesterday that he'd free you himself - if you became his wife. You have to answer both.
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.potter.success: Your master took the money without haggling. You left his house free and that same evening entered the potter's house as its mistress.
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.potter.failure: Your master took offense and sold you to an estate outside the city. The potter kept coming to the gate for a long time.
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.master.ok: He freed you before witnesses and called you his wife. Yesterday's kitchen companions bow to you now - and whisper behind your back.
ev.t_slave_freed_marriage.refuse.ok: You won't buy freedom at the price of yourself. The master scowls, the potter waits, and you save up on your own, scrap by scrap.
ev.t_master_heirs.title: Children of the First Marriage
ev.t_master_heirs.text: Your husband's grown children by his first wife declare that you bewitched their father for his money. They demand that a former slave know her place - and give back everything she got.
ev.t_master_heirs.court.success: Your husband came to court himself and said he chose you of his own free will. The suit was dismissed and your share confirmed before witnesses.
ev.t_master_heirs.court.failure: The court sided with the children. You had to give up half the property, and your name was dragged through the whole city.
ev.t_master_heirs.concede: Give up a share for peace
ev.t_master_heirs.concede.ok: You gave them the estate outside the city. The house is quieter, if not warmer.
ev.t_dowry_divorce.title: The Dowry
ev.t_dowry_divorce.text: You've found out that {npc} has squandered your dowry - on dice, debts and empty schemes. Your family puts it plainly: divorce, and demand your property back before it's too late. The law is on your side, but courts are slow.
ev.t_dowry_divorce.divorce.success: You returned to your family home with your dowry and your head held high. Free, with money - and with new thoughts about the future.
ev.t_dowry_divorce.divorce.failure: The divorce went through, but only a fraction came back. The neighbor women whisper that it was all your own fault.
ev.t_dowry_divorce.take_purse: Take the purse into your own hands
ev.t_dowry_divorce.take_purse.ok: The key to the strongbox now hangs at your belt. Your husband doesn't like it, but for the first time in years the household makes ends meet.
ev.t_dowry_divorce.endure: Endure it for peace at home
ev.t_dowry_divorce.endure.ok: You said nothing. {npc} promised to mend {g=npc_sex:his|her} ways - and you very much want to believe it.
ev.t_second_marriage.title: New Suitors
ev.t_second_marriage.text: A divorced woman with a dowry is a fine match, and the matchmakers soon come calling. An elderly, wealthy widower is asking for your hand - and so is a young craftsman of modest means you've had your eye on for a while.
ev.t_second_marriage.rich_widower.ok: A big house, a quiet life, a husband who doesn't interfere. Not love - but not a mistake either.
ev.t_second_marriage.for_love.ok: Less money, more laughter. For the first time you're marrying by your own choice, not by your fathers' agreement.
ev.t_second_marriage.stay_free.ok: You're mistress of your dowry and your days. Lonely sometimes - but no one will squander what's yours again.
ev.t_widowhood.title: Widowhood
ev.t_widowhood.text: {npc} died suddenly, within three days. After the funeral you're alone with the household, debts you never knew about, and a crowd at the door: some have come for money, others to propose.
ev.t_widowhood.run_business: Take the business into your own hands
ev.t_widowhood.run_business.success: You untangled the accounts, sacked a dishonest worker and went to the suppliers yourself. A year later the business earns more than it did under your husband.
ev.t_widowhood.run_business.failure: Debtors won't pay, workers steal, and merchants won't deal with a woman. You had to sell half of everything.
ev.t_widowhood.remarry.ok: Your husband's partner proposed marriage as a business deal. Debts settled, house saved - and feelings may come in time.
ev.t_widowhood.return_home: Go back to your parents' house
ev.t_widowhood.return_home.ok: You handed the household over to the creditors and went back to your own people. Poorer - but among familiar voices.
ev.t_poetess.title: Verses
ev.t_poetess.text: The verses you wrote for a friend's wedding are being sung all over the city. A wealthy connoisseur invites you to recite at his banquets, and your family is horrified: a respectable woman shouldn't have her name on everyone's lips.
ev.t_poetess.publish.success: Your verses are copied out and learned by heart. The best houses invite you, and even your family is proud now - out loud.
ev.t_poetess.publish.failure: The gossip was louder than the poems. People say all sorts of things about you, and not one word is about rhyme.
ev.t_poetess.under_his_name: Let a male relative recite them as his own
ev.t_poetess.under_his_name.ok: Your kinsman got the fame and the gifts; you got a share of the money and a quiet bitterness. At least he shares honestly.
ev.t_poetess.burn.ok: The hearth fire made short work of your poems. The lines still sound in your head, but soon they'll fade too.
ev.t_poems_live_on.title: Strangers' Voices
ev.t_poems_live_on.text: In a far-off land you heard travelers you'd never met singing your verses around a fire - with mistakes, in their own way, but yours. None of them knows who made them. And somehow that's the most beautiful part.
ev.t_youth_teacher.title: The Wandering Teacher
ev.t_youth_teacher.text: A wandering teacher - gray-haired, in worn-out shoes, with a bag of books - watched you argue with a merchant and invited you to come with him: to study, copy books, see the world. But your hands are needed at home, and your father has no love for bookish types.
ev.t_youth_teacher.ask_blessing.success: Your father was silent a long time, then said, “Just don't become one of those windbags.” A bundle was packed for you, and at dawn you left with the teacher.
ev.t_youth_teacher.ask_blessing.failure: Your father forbade you even to think of it. The teacher left alone, and you watched the road for a long time.
ev.t_youth_teacher.run_off: Slip away at night without asking
ev.t_youth_teacher.run_off.ok: You caught up with the teacher at the city gate. Ahead: books, arguments and new cities. Behind: a home where you won't soon be forgiven.
ev.t_youth_teacher.stay.ok: You walked the teacher to the crossroads. Your father clapped you on the shoulder like a grown-up for the first time.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.title: The Teacher's Legacy
ev.t_teacher_legacy.text: Your old teacher has died and left you everything he had: a chest of books, a threadbare cloak, and a dozen pupils who are now looking at you.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.open_school: Open a school of your own
ev.t_teacher_legacy.open_school.ok: You opened your doors to pupils. The pay is small, but boys from the neighboring quarters come to you and no one else.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.sell_library.ok: A book collector paid good money for them. The teacher would probably have winced - or perhaps laughed.
ev.t_teacher_legacy.donate: Give the books to a shrine's library
ev.t_teacher_legacy.donate.ok: Now many people read his books, and a tablet with his name stands on the shelf. Yours is there too, in smaller letters.
ev.t_plunder_share.title: The Fallen City
ev.t_plunder_share.text: The city has fallen after a long siege, and the commander has allowed plunder until morning. In the cellar of a rich house you find a woman with two children, clutching a casket to her chest. On the hill a temple is burning, and soldiers are already hauling out gold.
ev.t_plunder_share.take_casket.ok: You took the casket and left without looking back. There was gold in it. And that woman's eyes, which won't leave your memory.
ev.t_plunder_share.spare: Lead the family out of the city
ev.t_plunder_share.spare.ok: You led them through a breach in the wall to a grove outside the city. The woman pressed a ring into your hand and said something in her own language. The boy watched you go for a long time.
ev.t_plunder_share.loot_temple.ok: You carried a golden bowl and a fistful of jewels out of the temple. Wealth for life. They say foreign holy places know how to take revenge too.
ev.t_spared_family.title: The Boy from the Cellar
ev.t_spared_family.text: A young merchant came to your door and asked for you by name. He is the boy from the cellar in the fallen city. “Mother told me to find you,” he said. “She died blessing you.” He's carrying a purse and gifts.
ev.t_loot_curse.title: The Curse of Plunder
ev.t_loot_curse.text: Ever since you carried gold out of that temple, you dream of a burning hill. Misfortune follows misfortune, and the soothsayer put it bluntly: “The holy places of that city want what is theirs.”
ev.t_loot_curse.return_gold: Give the gold to a temple
ev.t_loot_curse.return_gold.ok: You gave most of the plunder to a temple. The dreams stopped, as if washed away by rain.
ev.t_loot_curse.sacrifice.ok: You prayed, gave offerings and hung up charms. It's a little easier - or so it seems.
ev.t_loot_curse.ignore.ok: You sent the soothsayer away. The dreams didn't stop, and your health began to fail too.
ev.t_grain_hoard.title: The Hungry Year
ev.t_grain_hoard.text: The harvest failed, grain shipments are late, and the price of bread has tripled. And your granaries are full. At the gate stand both speculators with fat purses and the hungry with empty baskets.
ev.t_grain_hoard.hoard: Hold the grain and sell high
ev.t_grain_hoard.hoard.success: You sold the grain at the highest price the city has ever seen. Your wealth grows, and someone writes unkind things about you in charcoal on the walls.
ev.t_grain_hoard.hoard.failure: A mob broke down the granary gates. Some of the grain was carried off, the rest burned, and you were nearly killed.
ev.t_grain_hoard.fair.ok: You sold at the old price until the grain ran out. A modest profit, but the city calls you an honest man.
ev.t_grain_hoard.donate.ok: You opened your granaries and handed out bread for a whole week. A city doesn't forget that.
ev.t_honorary_decree.title: The City's Honor
ev.t_honorary_decree.text: The city's elders have resolved to honor you: at every festival you now have a seat of honor, and a song has been made about that hungry year - with your name in it.
ev.t_big_commission.title: The Big Commission
ev.t_big_commission.text: The great sanctuary is looking for a workshop for an enormous commission - two years of work that will either make your name or ruin you. To take it on, you'll need to borrow for materials and hire hands.
ev.t_big_commission.borrow.success: Two sleepless years - and the work is done. It's shown to visitors, and you now have a workshop of your own with apprentices.
ev.t_big_commission.borrow.failure: Materials went up, workers drifted off, and the commission went to someone else. Only the debts remain.
ev.t_big_commission.partner: Take it on with your rival
ev.t_big_commission.partner.ok: You and your old rival split the work and the profit. Turns out you do better together than apart.
ev.t_big_commission.decline.ok: The commission went to another workshop. Safer - but in a couple of years you'll realize what you missed.
ev.t_commission_fame.title: A Master's Fame
ev.t_commission_fame.text: A distinguished traveler stood a long time before your work in the sanctuary, then sought out your workshop. “I want the same - for my own city,” he said, and laid down a deposit that took your breath away.
ev.t_adoption.title: Another Man's Name
ev.t_adoption.text: A rich, childless old man you've done business with offers to adopt you and make you his heir. You'd take his name and enter his family, and in the eyes of the law your own father would no longer be your father. Your father doesn't know yet.
ev.t_adoption.text.athens: A rich, childless old man you've done business with offers to adopt you so that his line and his household altars won't die out. You'd join his house and his deme, receive his whole fortune - and leave your own father's family. Your father doesn't know yet.
ev.t_adoption.accept.ok: The rite is done, the name changed. You have a big house, servants and fields. Your own father, when he heard, said nothing - he simply turned away.
ev.t_adoption.negotiate: Ask to keep ties with your own family
ev.t_adoption.negotiate.success: The old man thought it over and agreed: “Good that you don't forget your own.” You became his heir without losing your father.
ev.t_adoption.negotiate.failure: The old man took offense. “I need a son, not a guest.” A month later he adopted someone else.
ev.t_adoption.refuse.ok: You said you already have a father. When he heard, your father was lost for words for the first time you can remember.
ev.t_adoption_contest.title: The Nephews
ev.t_adoption_contest.text: Your adoptive father has died. His nephews, who waited all their lives for the inheritance, have gone to court: the adoption, they say, was a fraud, and the old man wasn't in his right mind.
ev.t_adoption_contest.court.success: Witnesses confirmed the old man was of sound mind. The court left everything to you and made the nephews pay the costs.
ev.t_adoption_contest.court.failure: The nephews found the right people. Half the inheritance went to them, and now you have a sworn enemy.
ev.t_adoption_contest.settle.ok: You set aside a share for them. The nephews left unhappy, but they've stopped suing.
ev.t_victor_honors.title: The Statue
ev.t_victor_honors.text: The city has set up your bronze statue by the stadium - young, swift, a wreath on its head. Boys touch its knees for luck, and you, gray-haired now, come by to look at the man you were.
